rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition attaches to ‘recounts’: the earth tells its news because its Lord inspired and commanded it to do so.
rows.anchor: معناه : تحدّث أخبارها بسبب إيحاء ربك لها ،   وأمره إياها بالتحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, she recounts by reporting that the Lord revealed her news; the revelation itself is her report of her news.
rows.anchor: تحديثها بأن ربك أوحى لها تحديث بأخبارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘that your Lord revealed’ is an apposition for ‘her news,’ since one may say both ‘told him this’ and ‘told him this about this.’
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ } بدلاً من { أَخْبَارَهَا } ،   كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Revealed to her’ means ‘revealed to it’; this is a figurative expression like God saying ‘Be, and it is.’
rows.anchor: و { أوحى لَهَا } بمعنى أوحى إليها ،   وهو مجاز

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud read ‘tُنَبِّئ أخبارها,’ with the earth informing of its news.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : «تنبىء أخبارها »

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr read ‘تنبئ’ with the light form.
rows.anchor: وسعيد بن جبير : تنبئ ،   بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation has people emerge from their graves for the gathering in separate groups: some with white faces and safety, others with black faces and terror.
rows.anchor: يصدرون عن مخارجهم من القبور إلى الموقف { أَشْتَاتاً } بيض الوجوه آمنين ؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they depart from the gathering in separate groups as the paths to Paradise and Hell divide, to see the recompense for their deeds.
rows.anchor: أو يصدرون عن الموقف أشتاتاً يتفرق بهم طريقا الجنة والنار ،   ليروا جزاء أعمالهم .

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s reading has the verb ‘ليَروا’ with fatḥa on its initial letter.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم : «ليَروا » بالفتح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن علي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Zayd ibn ʿAli read ‘يره’ with ḍamma on the initial letter.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وزيد بن علي : «يره » بالضم

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: An Arab rearranged ‘good, he will see’ in recitation; when corrected, he cited a verse showing that either side of Harsha is a road.
rows.anchor: ويحكى أنّ أعرابياً أخر { خَيْراً يَرَهُ } فقيل له : قدّمت وأخّرت ؛ فقال :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dharra is a small ant; another view identifies it as the dust mote visible in a sunbeam.
rows.anchor: والذرّة : النملة الصغيرة ،   وقيل : «الذرّ » ما يرى في شعاع الشمس من الهباء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reckoning of tiny good and evil deeds is resolved by applying the good deed to a member of the felicitous group.
rows.anchor: قلت : المعنى { فمن يعمل مثقال ذرّة خيراً } من فريق السعداء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tiny evil deed belongs to someone among the wretched, in light of the preceding description of people departing in distinct groups.
rows.anchor: ومن يعمل مثقال ذرّة شراً من فريق الأشقياء ؛ لأنه جاء بعد قوله : { يَصْدُرُ الناس أَشْتَاتاً } .

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises that reciting al-Zalzalah four times is like reciting the whole Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  من قرأ سورة إذا زلزلت أربع مرات كان كمن قرأ القرآن كله  "  .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathered host is one of the enemy gatherings, and ‘وسطه’ means that the raiders penetrated its midst.
rows.anchor: { جَمْعاً } من جموع الأعداء .   ووسطه بمعنى توسطه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘through it’ may refer to the place of the raid, or to the enemy indicated by ‘the chargers.’
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضمير لمكان الغارة .   وقيل : للعدوّ الذي دلّ عليه { والعاديات }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Al-naqʿ’ may mean clamour and shouting raised among the raided people.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالنقع : الصياح ،   من قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام :  "  ما لم يكن نقع ولا لقلقة  "  ،

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labīd uses ‘yanqaʿ’ for a sincere cry, supporting the gloss of al-naqʿ as a shout.
rows.anchor: وقول لبيد : فَمَتَى يَنْقَعْ صُراخٌ صَادِق ***

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywah reads ‘fa-aththarna’ with gemination, meaning they raised dust; taʾthīr carries the sense of making something appear.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة : «فأثرن » بالتشديد ،   بمعنى : فأظهرن به غباراً ؛ لأنّ التأثير فيه معنى الإظهار .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation reverses the letters of ‘thawwarna’ to ‘watharna’ and changes initial wāw to hamza.
rows.anchor: أو قلب ثورّن إلى وثرن ،   وقلب الواو همزة ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading geminates the verb to make it causative; the prefixed bāʾ is extra for emphasis and intensifies the meaning of entering the midst.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «فوسطن » بالتشديد للتعدية .   والباء مزيدة للتوكيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās first glossed the chargers as horses, but ʿAlī summoned him and challenged his uninformed answer, noting that Badr had only two horses.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : كنت جالساً في الحجر فجاء رجل فسألني عن { والعاديات ضَبْحاً ( 1 ) }

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī identified the chargers as camels travelling from ʿArafah to Muzdalifah and then Minā, and identified Jamʿ as Muzdalifah.
rows.anchor: فقال : ادعه لي ،   فلما وقفت على رأسه قال : تفتي الناس بما لا علم لك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the report is sound, ‘panting’ is transferred metaphorically to camels, just as bodily terms such as muzzle and hoof are transferred to humans.
rows.anchor: فإن صحّت الرواية فقد استعير الضبح للإبل ،   كما استعير المشافر والحافر للإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some hold that panting belongs only to horses, dogs, and foxes; another says it means the camels’ shoulders extending during travel, but that derivation is not established.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الضبح لا يكون إلاّ للفرس والكلب والثعلب .   وقيل : الضبح بمعنى الضبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is coordinated with the implied verbs replaced by the active participle: they ran, struck sparks, raided, and raised dust.
rows.anchor: قلت : على الفعل الذي وضع اسم الفاعل موضعه ؛ لأنّ المعنى : واللاتي عدون فأورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being witnesses his own ingratitude and cannot deny it because it is manifest.
rows.anchor: { وإنه } وإن الإنسان { على ذلك } على كنوده { لَشَهِيدٌ } يشهد على نفسه ،   ولا يقدر أن يجحده لظهور أمره .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God is witness to human ingratitude as a threat.
rows.anchor: وقيل : وإنّ الله على كنوده لشاهد على سبيل الوعيد .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Al-khayr’ means wealth, as in the verse concerning what someone leaves behind.
rows.anchor: { الخير } المال ،   من قوله تعالى : { إِن تَرَكَ خَيْرًا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Shadīd’ can mean miserly and withholding; loving wealth while finding spending burdensome makes him stingy.
rows.anchor: والشديد : البخيل الممسك .   يقال : فلان شديد ومتشدّد .

rows.speaker: طرفة
rows.claim: Ṭarafah’s verse uses ‘al-mutashaddid’ for the miserly man whose valuable property death selects.
rows.anchor: قال طرفة : أَرَى الْمَوْتَ يَعْتَامُ الْكِرَامَ وَيَصْطَفِي ***

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he is strong in loving wealth, preferring worldly life and pursuing it, but weak and sluggish in worshipping God and thanking Him.
rows.anchor: أو أراد بالشديد : القوي ،   وإنه لحب المال وإيثار الدنيا وطلبها قوي مطيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he is constricted and closed in his love of good things, rather than open and expansive.
rows.anchor: أو أراد : أنه لحب الخيرات غير هش منبسط ،   ولكنه شديد منقبض .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Buʿthira’ means that the dead are raised; variant readings include ‘baḥthara’ and two forms of ‘baḥatha/baḥthara.’
rows.anchor: { بُعْثِرَ } بعث .   وقرىء : «بحثر » ،   وبحث ،   وبحثر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb has active-voice readings in both its forms, as well as a light, ungeminated reading.
rows.anchor: وحصل : على بنائهما للفاعل .   وحصل : بالتخفيف .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb can mean gathering the inner contents in records and exposing them as a collected whole.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ( حصلّ ) جمع في الصحف ،   أي : أظهر محصلاً مجموعاً .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the contents are sorted into good and evil.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ميز بين خيره وشره .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s being fully informed of them on Judgment Day means He recompenses them according to their deeds, the effect of His knowledge.
rows.anchor: ومعنى علمه بهم يوم القيامة : مجازاته لهم على مقادير أعمالهم ؛ لأنّ ذلك أثر خبره بهم .

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abū al-Sammāl reads the verse without the emphatic lām: ‘inna rabbahum bihim yawmaʾidhin khabīr.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال : «إن ربهم بهم يومئذ خبير » .

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report promises ten good deeds per person who spent the night at Muzdalifah and attended Jamʿ to whoever recites al-ʿĀdiyāt.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم :  " من قرأ سورة والعاديات أعطي من الأجر عشر حسنات بعدد من بات بالمزدلفة وشهد جمعاً  "  .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains resemble dyed wool because they have varied colors and fluffed wool because their parts disperse.
rows.anchor: وشبه الجبال بالعهن وهو الصوف المصبغ ألواناً ؛

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads ‘ka-l-ṣūf’ instead of ‘ka-l-ʿihn.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : «كالصوف » .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Kallā’ rebukes and alerts observers not to make worldly life their entire concern while neglecting religion.
rows.anchor: { كَلاَّ } ردع وتنبيه على أنه لا ينبغي للناظر لنفسه أن تكون الدنيا جميع همه ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You will know’ is a warning meant to make them fear and awaken from heedlessness.
rows.anchor: { سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ } إنذار ليخافوا فيتنبهوا من غفلتهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the warning strengthens both the rebuke and threat; ‘then’ marks the second warning as more forceful, like repeating an admonition.
rows.anchor: والتكرير : تأكيد للردع والإنذار عليهم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will recognize their error when they witness the terror awaiting them in the encounter with God; this warning is counsel and mercy.
rows.anchor: سوف تعلمون الخطأ فيما أنتم عليه إذا عاينتم ما قدامكم من هول لقاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional ‘if you knew’ has an omitted answer: certain knowledge of what lies ahead, like the matters on which they focus their efforts, would lead them to indescribable action; they are heedless and ignorant.
rows.anchor: وقال : { لَّوْ تَعْلَمُونَ } محذوف الجواب ،   يعني : لو تعلمون ما بين أيديكم علم الأمر اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming Hellfire specifies what the warning threatened; clarifying after an ambiguous threat magnifies and makes it awesome.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : { لَتَرَوُنَّ الجحيم ( 6 ) } فبين لهم ما أنذرهم منه وأوعدهم به ؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement answers an omitted oath, whose purpose is to make the threat certain beyond doubt.
rows.anchor: وهو جواب قسم محذوف ،   والقسم لتوكيد الوعيد ،   وأن ما أوعدوا به ما لا مدخل فيه للريب ؛

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the threat with ‘then’ intensifies the warning and increases its terror.
rows.anchor: وكرره معطوفا بثم تغليظا في التهديد وزيادة في التهويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamzated reading ‘latarʾun’ is disliked because the wāw’s ḍamma is only incidental from meeting two quiescent letters, unlike the regular case.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «لترؤن » بالهمز ،   وهي مستكرهة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings have ‘you will see’ or ‘you will see it’ in the passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقرىء لترون ولترونها على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The eye of certainty’ means sight that is itself the essence and purest form of certainty.
rows.anchor: { عَيْنَ اليقين } أي : الرؤية التي هي نفس اليقين وخالصته .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing may mean either knowledge or visual perception.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالرؤية : العلم والإبصار .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing in question is amusement and indulgence that distract a person from religion and its obligations.
rows.anchor: { عَنِ النعيم } عن اللهو والتنعم الذي شغلكم الالتذاذ به عن الدين وتكاليفه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke concerns people devoted to pleasures, fine food and clothes, and entertainment who neglect knowledge and work instead of enduring their burdens.
rows.anchor: قلت : هو نعيم من عكف همته على استيفاء اللذات ،   ولم يعش إلاّ ليأكل الطيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who use God’s provisions to pursue knowledge and work and rise in gratitude are exempt from that rebuke; the Prophet and companions praised God after dates and water.
rows.anchor: فأما من تمتع بنعمة الله وأرزاقه التي لم يخلقها إلاّ لعباده ،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After eating dates and drinking water with his companions, the Prophet praised God for feeding and giving them drink and making them Muslims.
rows.anchor: فقال : « الحمد لله الذي أطعمنا وسقانا وجعلنا مسلمين  » .

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A merit report says al-Takāthur’s reciter is spared accounting for worldly blessings and receives the reward of reciting a thousand verses.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : « من قرأ ( ألهاكم التكاثر ) لم يحاسبه الله بالنعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘In misguidance’ means waste and nullification; the idiom ‘he led his plot astray’ means he made it futile.
rows.anchor: { فِى تَضْلِيلٍ } في تضييع وإبطال .   يقال : ضلل كيده ،   إذا جعله ضالاً ضائعاً .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression ‘misguided king’ for Imruʾ al-Qays refers to his wasting his father’s kingdom; the verse links to the phrase about disbelievers’ plots in error.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : { وَمَا كَيْدُ الكافرين إِلاَّ فِى ضلال } [ غافر : 25 ] وقيل : لامريء القيس : الملك الضليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They first tried to divert pilgrims from the Kaaba by building al-Qullays, but God thwarted the plot by sending fire; their later plan to demolish it was defeated by the birds.
rows.anchor: يعني : أنهم كادوا البيت أوّلاً ببناء القليس ،   وأرادوا أن ينسخوا أمره بصرف وجوه الحاج إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Abābīl’ means flocks; its singular is ‘ibālah,’ a large bundle, and clustered flocks resemble bundles; a proverb says one bundle atop another.
rows.anchor: { أَبَابِيلَ } حزائق ،   الواحدة : إبالة .   وفي أمثالهم : ضغث على إبالة ،   وهي : الحزمة الكبيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘abābīl’ has no singular, like ‘ʿabādīd’ and ‘shamāṭīṭ.’
rows.anchor: وقيل : أبابيل مثل عباديد ،   وشماطيط ،   لا واحد لها .

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfah reads ‘yarmīhim’ in the masculine because ‘ṭayr’ is a masculine collective noun, though it is feminized according to its meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حنيفة رحمه الله : «يرميهم » أي : الله تعالى أو الطير ؛ لأنه اسم جمع مذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Sijjīl’ may be the name of the register containing the written punishment of disbelievers, just as ‘sijjīn’ names their deeds register; its root may be ‘isjāl,’ dispatching punishment.
rows.anchor: وسجيل : كأنه علم للديوان الذي كتب فيه عذاب الكفار ،   كما أن سجيناً علم لديوان أعمالهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the stones as baked clay, like bricks are baked.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : من طين مطبوخ كما يطبخ الآجر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats ‘sijjīl’ as an Arabicized Persian expression.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو معرب من سنككل .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another gloss derives it from severe punishment and cites a line attributed to Ibn Muqbil, but the poem actually reads ‘sijjīnā,’ so it does not establish ‘sijjīl.’
rows.anchor: وقيل : من شديد عذابه ؛ ورووا بيت ابن مقبل :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were likened to crop leaves eaten away, that is, damaged by feeding insects.
rows.anchor: وشبهوا بورق الزرع إذا أكل ،   أي : وقع فيه الأكال .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Eaten’ may mean eaten by worms, or straw eaten and excreted by livestock; the latter wording follows Qurʾanic decorum, as in the verse saying the two ate food.
rows.anchor: أي : وقع فيه الأكال ،   وهو أن يأكله الدود .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the grain was eaten, leaving only an empty husk.
rows.anchor: أو أريد : أكل حبه فبقي صفراً منه .

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A merit report says reciting al-Fīl protects a person during life from being swallowed by the earth or transformed.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الفيل أعفاه الله أيام حياته من الخسف والمسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary meaning of ‘wa-nḥar’ is slaughtering sacrificial camels.
rows.anchor: والنحر : نحر البدن ؛ وعن عطية

rows.speaker: عطية
rows.claim: ʿAṭiyyah interprets it as performing dawn prayer at Jamʿ and sacrifice at Minā.
rows.anchor: وعن عطية : هي صلاة الفجر بجمع ،   والنحر بمنى .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations are the Eid prayer with sacrifice, prayer in general, and placing the right hand over the left.
rows.anchor: وقيل : صلاة العيد والتضحية .   وقيل : هي جنس الصلاة .   والنحر : وضع اليمين على الشمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God gave the Prophet incomparable abundance in both worlds, he should worship, pray, and sacrifice in God’s name, opposing the people who sacrifice to idols and relying on his divine benefactor.
rows.anchor: فاعبد ربك الذي أعزّك بإعطائه ،   وشرفك وصانك من منن الخلق ،   مراغماً لقومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who hates the Prophet is the cut-off one, not the Prophet: believers descend from him, his name endures in worship and learning, and he has indescribable reward in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: من أبغضك من قومك لمخالفتك لهم { هُوَ الأبتر } لا أنت ؛ لأنّ كل من يولد إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s enemy is forgotten in this life and the next, or remembered only with curses; therefore he, not the Prophet, is truly cut off.
rows.anchor: وإنما الأبتر هو شانئك المنسي في الدنيا والآخرة ،   وإن ذكر ذكر باللعن .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called Muḥammad ‘ṣanbūr,’ claiming his memory would die when he died.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يقولون : إنّ محمداً صنبور : إذا مات مات ذكره .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says the sūrah was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who called the Prophet cut off; ‘abtar’ means a person without descendants.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في العاص بن وائل ،   وقد سماه الأبتر ،   والأبتر : الذي لا عقب له .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word also describes a donkey without a tail.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحمار الأبتر الذي لا ذنب له

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A merit report hopes that anyone reciting al-Kawthar will be given drink from every river in Paradise and reward for each sacrifice offered on the Day of Sacrifice.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الكوثر سقاه الله من كل نهر في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb after ‘lā’ is future; ‘mā’ normally governs an imperfect in the present, while ‘lan’ intensifies the negation expressed by ‘lā.’ Khalīl says ‘lan’ derives from ‘lā an.’
rows.anchor: لأنّ «لا » لا تدخل إلاّ على مضارع في معنى الاستقبال ،   كما أن «ما » لا تدخل إلاّ على مضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mutual refusal concerns future worship: the Prophet will not worship their gods, and they will not worship his God.
rows.anchor: المعنى : لا أفعل في المستقبل ما تطلبونه مني من عبادة آلهتكم ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction means he had never worshipped what they worshipped, even before the mission; how could they expect him to do so in Islam?
rows.anchor: أي : وما كنت قطّ عابداً فيما سلف ما عبدتم فيه .   يعني : لم تعهد مني عبادة صنم في الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have not worshipped what the Prophet worships during the period when he worships it.
rows.anchor: أي : وما عبدتم في وقت ما أنا على عبادته .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording uses the past for their idol worship because they worshipped idols before the mission, while the Prophet did not then worship God.
rows.anchor: قلت : لأنهم كانوا يعبدون الأصنام قبل المبعث ،   وهو لم يكن يعبد الله تعالى في ذلك الوقت .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Mā’ rather than ‘man’ points to the quality worshipped: the Prophet rejects falsehood and they reject truth.
rows.anchor: قلت : لأن المراد الصفة ،   كأنه قال : لا أعبد الباطل ،   ولا تعبدون الحق .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘mā’ is a verbal noun: he rejects their worship and they reject his worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن «ما » مصدرية ،   أي : لا أعبد عبادتكم ،   ولا تعبدون عبادتي .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees retain their polytheism while the Prophet holds to monotheism; as a prophet inviting them to truth and salvation, he tells them to leave him alone if they refuse and stop summoning him to shirk.
rows.anchor: لكم شرككم ،   ولي توحيدي .   والمعنى : أني نبيّ مبعوث إليكم لأدعوكم إلى الحق والنجاة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A merit report compares reciting al-Kāfirūn to a quarter of the Qurʾan and promises distance from rebellious devils, freedom from shirk, and safety from the greatest terror.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  من قرأ ( سورة الكافرون ) فكأنما قرأ ربع القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘In crowds’ means dense groups: whole tribes entered together after people had entered singly or in pairs.
rows.anchor: أَفْوَاجاً } جماعات كثيفة كانت تدخل فيه القبيلة بأسرها ،

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jābir wept because he heard the Prophet say that people would enter God’s religion in groups and later leave it in groups.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه : أنه بكى ذات يوم ،   فقيل له ،   فقال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the people entering in crowds as the people of Yemen.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أراد بالناس أهل اليمن .

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayrah reports that on revelation the Prophet announced the victory and arrival of Yemenis, praised their tender hearts and Yemeni faith, jurisprudence, and wisdom, and said their advance came from Yemen.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة : لما نزلت ،   قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  الله أكبر ،   جاء نصر الله والفتح ،   وجاء أهل اليمن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that after Mecca fell, Arabs recognized that the Prophet could not be resisted after victory over the sanctuary; God had protected it from the Elephant army and others, so tribes entered Islam without fighting.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : لما فتح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مكة أقبلت العرب بعضها على بعض ،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās read the opening as ‘fatḥu Allāhi wa-l-naṣr.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس : ( فتح الله والنصر ) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads ‘yudkhalūn’ in the passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «يدخلون » على البناء للمفعول .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They enter’ is accusative as a circumstantial clause if ‘you saw’ means saw or recognized, or it is a second object if ‘saw’ means knew.
rows.anchor: قلت : النصب إما على الحال ،   على أن رأيت بمعنى أبصرت ،   أو عرفت .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command can mean proclaiming God’s transcendence while praising Him and marveling at how He enabled an unexpected conquest of the sanctuary; praise Him for His action.
rows.anchor: فقل سبحان الله ،   حامداً له ،   أي : فتعجب لتيسير الله ما لم يخطر ببالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, remember God in praise and add to worship and praise in gratitude for increased blessings.
rows.anchor: أو : فاذكره مسبحاً حامداً ،   زيادة في عبادته والثناء عليه ،   لزيادة إنعامه عليك .

rows.speaker: أم هانئ
rows.claim: Umm Hāniʾ reports that after Mecca was conquered the Prophet prayed eight cycles of the forenoon prayer at the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: روت أمّ هانيء أنه لما فتح باب الكعبة صلى صلاة الضحى ثماني ركعات .

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾishah says that before his death the Prophet frequently said, ‘Glory be to You, O God, with Your praise; I ask Your forgiveness and repent to You.’
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة : كان عليه الصلاة والسلام يكثر قبل موته أن يقول :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairing glorification with asking forgiveness completes religious duty by combining obedience and avoiding sin; for the infallible Prophet it gently teaches his community, and seeking forgiveness is itself humility and worship.
rows.anchor: والأمر بالاستغفار مع التسبيح تكميل للأمر بما هو قوام أمر الدين : من الجمع بين الطاعة والاحتراس من المعصية

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that he sought God’s forgiveness one hundred times in a day and night.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  إني لأستغفر في اليوم والليلة مائة مرة

rows.speaker: العباس
rows.claim: When the Prophet recited the sūrah to his companions, they rejoiced but al-ʿAbbās wept, saying that the Prophet’s death had been announced; the Prophet agreed and lived two years without joyful laughter.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنه لما قرآها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم على أصحابه استبشروا ،   وبكى العباس ،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another account says Ibn ʿAbbās, rather than al-ʿAbbās, inferred the Prophet’s death; the Prophet praised the young man’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن ابن عباس هو الذي قال ذلك ؛ فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: At ʿUmar’s council with the veterans of Badr, some said the sūrah orders praise, forgiveness, and repentance after victory; Ibn ʿAbbās instead interpreted it as announcing the Prophet’s death, and ʿUmar affirmed his insight.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن عمر رضي الله عنهما كان يدنيه ،   ويأذن له مع أهل بدر ،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Another report says the Prophet announced that a servant was offered a choice between this world and meeting God and chose meeting God; Abū Bakr understood and offered his family and wealth in ransom.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنها لما نزلت خطب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال :

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Fāṭimah not to cry because she would be the first of his family to join him after his death had been intimated to him.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : أنه دعا فاطمة رضي الله عنها فقال :

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd called the sūrah the Farewell Sūrah.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود أن هذه السورة تسمى سورة التوديع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has always accepted penitents who seek forgiveness; every person seeking forgiveness should expect that same response.
rows.anchor: أي : كان في الأزمنة الماضية منذ خلق المكلفين تواباً عليهم إذا استغفروا ،   فعلى كل مستغفر أن يتوقع مثل ذلك .

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A merit report promises a reward like witnessing the conquest of Mecca with Muḥammad to anyone who recites the sūrah.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة إذا جاء نصر الله أعطي من الأجر كمن شهد مع محمد يوم فتح مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Mā aghnā’ is either an interrogative with a force of denial in the accusative, or a negation; ‘mā kasaba’ is nominative.
rows.anchor: { مَا أغنى } استفهام في معنى الإنكار ،   ومحله النصب أو نفي { وَمَا كَسَبَ } مرفوع .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Mā kasaba’ may be a relative or a verbal noun, meaning what he acquired or his earning.
rows.anchor: وما موصولة أو مصدرية بمعنى : ومكسوبه .   أو : وكسبه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean his money and profits, his livestock and their offspring and benefits, his inherited wealth and personal earnings, or his old and newly acquired wealth.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : لم ينفعه ماله وما كسب بماله ،   يعني : رأس المال والأرباح .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets ‘what he earned’ as his children.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : ما كسب ولده .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A family dispute anecdote says Abū Lahab called his children ‘filthy earnings’ after one shoved him while he broke up their fight; a Prophetic report says a man’s child counts among his earnings.
rows.anchor: وحكي أن بني أبي لهب احتكموا إليه ،   فاقتتلوا ،   فقام يحجز بينهم ،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that a man’s best food is what he earns and that his child is among his earnings.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام :  "  إن أطيب ما يأكل الرجل من كسبه ،

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes the phrase to mean wealth and wicked work, specifically Abū Lahab’s plot against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك : ما ينفعه ماله وعمله الخبيث ،   يعني كيده في عداوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah interprets it as work he thought would benefit him, linking it to the verse about deeds made like scattered dust.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : عمله الذي ظنّ أنه منه على شيء ،   كقوله : { وَقَدِمْنَا إلى مَا عَمِلُواْ مِنْ عَمَلٍ } [ الفرقان : 23 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Lahab reportedly boasted that if his nephew were right, he could ransom himself from the punishment with his wealth and children.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه كان يقول : إن كان ما يقول ابن أخي حقاً فأنا أفتدي منه نفسي بمالي وولدي .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read with fatḥa or ḍamma on its initial yāʾ, either lightly or with gemination; the future particle marks an inevitable threat, though its time is delayed.
rows.anchor: «سيصلى » قرىء : بفتح الياء وبضمها مخففاً ومشدداً ،   والسين للوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wife is Umm Jamīl bint Ḥarb, Abū Sufyān’s sister; she carried thorns and saʿdān and scattered them by the Prophet’s path at night.
rows.anchor: { وامرأته } هي أم جميل بنت حرب أخت أبي سفيان ،   وكانت تحمل حزمة من الشوك والحسك والسعدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, she spread malicious gossip; calling such a person a carrier of firewood means that she kindles discord and causes evil between people.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانت تمشى بالنميمة .   ويقال للمشاء بالنمائم المفسد بين الناس : يحمل الحطب بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet’s ‘wet firewood’ signifies smoking and hence greater discord and harm.
rows.anchor: جعله رطبا ليدل على التدخين الذي هو زيادة في الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘His wife’ is nominative by coordination with the pronoun in ‘he will roast’: he and his wife will burn.
rows.anchor: ورفعت عطفاً على الضمير في { سيصلى } أي : سيصلى هو وامرأته .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘In her neck’ is either a circumstantial phrase or a subject, with ‘a rope’ as its predicate.
rows.anchor: و { فِى جِيدِهَا } في موضع الحال ،   أو على الابتداء ،   وفي جيدها : الخبر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading ‘ḥammālata l-ḥaṭab’ is an insult, and the author prefers it because the Prophet was praised by the gracious feature of insulting Umm Jamīl.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : «حمالة الحطب » بالنصب على الشتم ؛ وأنا أستحب هذه القراءة ،   وقد توسل إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings include the nominative or accusative with tanwīn and a diminutive form ‘wa-muraytahu.’
rows.anchor: «حمالة الحطب » و«حمالة للحطب » : بالتنوين ،   بالرفع والنصب .   وقرىء : «ومريته » بالتصغير .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Masad’ is tightly twisted cord made from palm fiber, leather, or another material; ‘mamsūd’ also describes a firmly corded physique, as the verse illustrates.
rows.anchor: المسد : الذي فتل من الحبال فتلاً شديداً ،   من ليف كان أو جلد ،   أو غيرهما .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She ties her thorn bundle to her neck like a lowly wood carrier, humiliating her despite her household’s high rank and provoking her and her husband.
rows.anchor: وأنها تحمل تلك الحزمة من الشوك وتربطها في جيدها كما يفعل الحطابون : تخسيساً لحالها ،   وتحقيراً لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verse ridicules al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās for the insult about the wood-carrier; he answers by invoking his mother’s noble lineage.
rows.anchor: ولقد عير بعض الناس الفضل بن العباس بن عتبة ابن أبي لهب بحمالة الحطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, she will remain in Hell carrying firewood from the tree of Zaqqūm or Ḍarīʿ on her back and wearing a fire chain, punished in a form matching her crime.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى : أنّ حالها تكون في نار جهنم على الصورة التي كانت عليها حين كانت تحمل حزمة الشوك

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A merit report hopes that God will not house the reciter of Sūrat Tabbat with Abū Lahab.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  من قرأ سورة ( تبت ) رجوت أن لا يجمع الله بينه وبين أبي لهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil in creation includes sins and harms people inflict on one another, harms animals inflict through eating or biting, and harms placed in inanimate things, such as fire burning and poison killing.
rows.anchor: وشرّهم : ما يفعله المكلفون من الحيوان من المعاصي والمآثم ،   ومضارة بعضهم بعضاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Ghāsiq’ is the night once darkness deepens, linked to the verse about nightfall; the eye fills with tears and a wound with blood, while ‘waqab’ means darkness entering everything or the sun setting.
rows.anchor: والغاسق : الليل إذا اعتكر ظلامه من قوله تعالى : { إلى غسق الليل } [ الإسراء : 78 ] ،

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet called sunset the time when the evening prayer becomes due.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : لما رأى الشمس قد وقبت قال : « هذا حين حلها ،   يعني صلاة المغرب  »

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾishah says the Prophet pointed to the moon and told her to seek refuge from its evil as it entered an eclipse and darkened.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها : أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيدي فأشار إلى القمر فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the dark one is a black snake, and ‘waqab’ means its strike or penetration; ‘waqb’ means a hole, as in the word for a serving bowl’s hollow.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالغاسق : الأسود من الحيات ،   ووقبه : ضربه ونقبه .   والوقب : النقب .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is feared because harm spreads more widely then and is harder to avoid; its evil is associated with the time in which it occurs.
rows.anchor: والتعوّذ من شرّ الليل ؛ لأن انبثاثه فيه أكثر ،   والتحرّز منه أصعب .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘blowers’ can be women, souls, or groups of sorceresses who tie thread knots, blow over them, and recite spells; blowing is a breath mixed with saliva.
rows.anchor: { النفاثات } النساء ،   أو النفوس ،   أو الجماعات السواحر اللاتي يعقدن عقداً في خيوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blowing spells has no causal effect; harm can occur if a harmful substance is fed, given to drink or smell, or brought into contact with the bewitched person. God may act then as a test, while ignorant commoners attribute effects to sorceresses and the steadfast do not.
rows.anchor: ولا تأثير لذلك ،   اللهم إلاّ إذا كان ثم إطعام شيء ضار ،   أو سقيه ،   أو إشمامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge may mean asking protection from their practice of magic and the sin they commit by it.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن يستعاذ من عملهن الذي هو صنعة السحر ومن إثمهنّ في ذلك .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation seeks refuge from their tempting people while blowing spells; they may be scheming women, as in the verse about women’s great guile, or women whose beauty bewitches men.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يستعاذ من فتنتهنّ الناس عند نفثهن ،   ويجوز أن يراد بهنّ النساء الكيادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘When he envies’ means when envy becomes visible and he acts to harm the envied person; if its effect stays hidden, it harms only the envious person.
rows.anchor: { إِذَا حَسَدَ } إذا ظهر حسده ،   وعمل بمقتضاه : من بغي الغوائل للمحسود ؛ لأنه إذا لم يظهر أثر ما أضمره

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz says he has seen no oppressor more like an oppressed person than an envious man.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن عبد العزيز : لم أر ظالماً أشبه بالمظلوم من حاسد ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the harm is the envious person’s sin and ugliness when envying and displaying its effects.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بشرّ الحاسد : إثمه وسماجة حاله في وقت حسده ،   وإظهاره أثره .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the first verse generalizes every evil, these dangers are singled out because they are hidden and befall people from where they cannot see, like an ambush.
rows.anchor: قلت : قد خص شرّ هؤلاء من كلّ شر لخفاء أمره ،   وأنه يلحق الإنسان من حيث لا يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blowers are definite because every sorceress is harmful; the night and the envious are indefinite because only some nights and envies cause harm.
rows.anchor: قلت : عرفت النفاثات ؛ لأن كل نفاثة شريرة ،   ونكر غاسق ؛ لأنّ كل غاسق لا يكون فيه الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Envy for good qualities may be praiseworthy, unlike harmful envy, as in the saying that there is no envy except in two cases.
rows.anchor: وكذلك كل حاسد لا يضرّ .   ورب حسد محمود ،   وهو الحسد في الخيرات .

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says there is no envy except in two cases.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : « لا حسد إلاّ في اثنتين  » ،

rows.speaker: أبو تمام
rows.claim: Abū Tammām’s verse says one who envies noble qualities is not truly an envious person.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو تمام : وَمَا حَاسِدٌ فِي الْمَكْرُمَاتِ بِحَاسِدِ***

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further poetic line says that envy of excellence is beautiful among its peers.
rows.anchor: وقال : إنَّ الْعُلاَ حَسَنٌ فِي مِثْلِهَا الْحَسَدُ .   .   .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘King of people’ and ‘God of people’ are explanatory appositions to ‘Lord of people,’ like a name followed by clarifying titles.
rows.anchor: قلت : هما عطف بيان ،   كقولك : سيرة أبي حفص عمر الفاروق .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Lord of people’ needs clarification because ‘lord’ can describe others, as the verse says of rabbis and monks, and ‘king’ can also describe other beings.
rows.anchor: لأنه قد يقال لغيره : رب الناس ،   كقوله : { اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أَرْبَاباً مّن دُونِ الله } [ التوبة : 31 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘God of people’ is uniquely specific to God and has no partner, making it the final clarification.
rows.anchor: وأما { إله الناس } فخاص لا شركة فيه ،   فجعل غاية للبيان .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ‘people’ is repeated instead of replaced by a pronoun because appositional clarification calls for explicit mention.
rows.anchor: قلت : لأنّ عطف البيان للبيان ،   فكان مظنة للإظهار دون الإضمار .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Waswās’ is a noun meaning whispering, like ‘zalzāl’ means shaking; its verbal noun has kasra. The word refers to Satan, named for his work, or to a possessor of whispers; whispering is a hidden sound like jewelry’s soft noise.
rows.anchor: { الوسواس } اسم بمعنى الوسوسة ،   كالزلزال بمعنى الزلزلة .   وأمّا المصدر فوسواس بالكسر كزلزال .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Khannās’ means one who habitually retreats, formed from khunūs, withdrawal.
rows.anchor: و { الخناس } الذي عادته أن يخنس ،   منسوب إلى الخنوس ،   وهو التأخر ،

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Satan withdraws when a person remembers God and whispers when that person is heedless.
rows.anchor: لما روي عن سعيد بن جبير : إذا ذكر الإنسان ربه خنس الشيطان وولى ،   فإذا غفل وسوس إليه .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun may be genitive as an adjective, or nominative or accusative as an invective; on an invective reading the reciter may pause at ‘al-khannās’ and start anew at ‘alladhī.’
rows.anchor: { الذى يُوَسْوِسُ } يجوز في محله الحركات الثلاث ،   فالجر على الصفة ،   والرفع والنصب على الشتم ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase explains the whisperer: Satan comes in two kinds, from jinn and humans, as the phrase ‘devils of humans and jinn’ says.
rows.anchor: { مِنَ الجنة والناس } بيان للذي يوسوس ،   على أن الشيطان ضربان : جنى وإنسي ،

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abū Dharr asked a man whether he had sought refuge from a human Satan.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال لرجل : هل تعوذت بالله من شيطان الإنس ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘min’ attaches to ‘whispers’: whispering reaches people from the direction of jinn and from the direction of humans.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( من ) متعلقاً ب( يوسوس ) ،   ومعناه : ابتداء الغاية ،   أي : يوسوس في صدروهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take jinn and humans as an explanation of ‘people,’ since the word may include jinn, citing ‘nafar’ and ‘men’ in Sūrat al-Jinn.
rows.anchor: وقيل : من الجنّة والناس بيان للناس ،   وأن اسم الناس ينطلق على الجنة ،   واستدلّوا ( بنفر ) و ( رجال ) في سورة الجن .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That reading is unsuitable to Qurʾanic eloquence: jinn are hidden beings while nās are visible, from seeing, like bashar; calling both groups nās would sound affected.
rows.anchor: وما أحقه ؛ لأن الجن سموا «جنا » لاجتنانهم ،   والناس «ناساً » لظهورهم ،   من الإيناس وهو الإبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Better, ‘people’ means the forgetful, as in the cited verses; jinn and humans then explain it because both kinds forget God’s right.
rows.anchor: وأجود منه أن يراد بالناس : الناسي ،   كقوله : { يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الداع } [ القمر : 6 ] كما قرىء : { مِنْ حَيْثُ أَفَاضَ الناس } [ البقرة : 199 ]

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls the two protective sūrahs unlike any others and especially beloved and pleasing to God; these are the two Muʿawwidhatayn, also called al-Muqashqishatān.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  لقد أنزلت عليّ سورتان ما أنزل مثلهما ،   وإنك لن تقرأ سورتين أحب ولا أرضى عند الله منهما
